title: How to Clean a Gas Stove

seo.title: How to Clean a Gas Stove
seo.meta_description: Clean a gas stove with cool burners, without soaking igniters or blocking burner ports. Dry and reassemble every part correctly before lighting it.
seo.search_intent: Clean a gas range or cooktop without getting igniters wet, altering burner ports, or reassembling burner parts incorrectly.

excerpt: On a gas stove, cleaning is not finished when the grease is gone. Burner caps and heads must also be dry, unobstructed, and seated correctly before ignition.
content_html:
Turn every control off and let the cooktop cool completely. If the range uses electric ignition, follow the manual for disconnecting power. Never clean around a lit burner.

Remove grates and approved burner parts

Take a photo first if several burner assemblies look alike. Wash only parts the manufacturer says can be washed, and keep caps matched to their positions.

Degrease the surface without flooding it

Apply cleaner to the cloth or sponge, especially near igniters and openings. Lift softened grease with nonabrasive tools.

Keep burner ports clear

Food debris can distort the flame pattern. Use only the cleaning method the manufacturer recommends; do not enlarge ports with drill bits or oversized needles.

Dry thoroughly before reassembly

A wet burner can ignite poorly or click continuously. Center each cap so it sits flat and stable before testing.

Watch the flame afterward

A very uneven flame, flame emerging from the wrong area, or a burner that will not stay lit after correct drying and assembly needs service. If you smell unburned gas, turn the control off, avoid operating electrical switches, ventilate as directed, and follow your gas utility’s emergency procedure.

Frequent light cleaning is much safer and easier than scraping carbonized grease from around sensitive ignition components.

faq.question: Can I soak the burners?
faq.answer: Only if the manufacturer permits it. Igniters and some burner components should not be soaked.

faq.question: Why is the stove clicking after cleaning?
faq.answer: Moisture or a misseated burner cap can cause repeated ignition clicking. Let parts dry and verify assembly.

faq.question: What if I smell gas?
faq.answer: Stop trying to ignite the burner, turn it off, avoid sparks and switches, and follow your gas utility’s emergency instructions.
